newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem sees profit improvement in '97.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem sees profit improvement in '97.

text.p: Restructuring actions taken last year at Bethlehem Steel Corp should help the company improve profitability in 1997, Bethlehem Steel Chairman Hank Barnette said Wednesday.
"We expect the actions we took in '96 will improve profitability in '97, which in turn strengthens and increases the value of the company," Barnette said in a conference call with reporters.
Earlier Wednesday, Bethlehem Steel posted a fourth quarter loss of $3.19 per share versus earnings of $0.20 per share in the year-earlier period.

The '96 quarter included restructuring charges totaling $450 million before taxes. The company late last year announced it would attempt to sell Bethlehem Structural Products, BethForge, Centec and BethShip.
Those operations have been posting consecutive losses for several quarters.
Efforts to sell Bethlehem Structural Products were unsuccessful and Bethlehem Steel said recently the operation will close in the first quarter.
Efforts to sell the remaining divisions are ongoing, Barnette said.
"We are in negotiations with qualified buyers," he said. He declined to identify the potential buyers and declined to comment on how close the parties may be to reaching sales agreements.
Separately, Barnette declined to comment on steel pricing in '97. Prices fell about three percent last year from '95 levels.
"It's early (in the year,") he said. "Let us get through the first quarter...and then talk about how '97 looks (in terms of pricing,") he said.
Barnette said steel demand should be strong this year and industry shipments should be close to 100 million tons, about the level shipped last year.
